docs.title: Cobblemon Action Combat
docs.text:
Not released yet

Action Combat has no public download yet. These pages describe the current development build, 0.1.41, which has every feature planned for 1.0.0 and is being play-tested. Anything not described here is not in the mod yet.

docs.title: Cobblemon Action Combat
docs.text:
Cobblemon's battles, played in real time. When a fight starts you become your Pokémon: you run it at its own Speed, cast its four moves on the number keys, dodge, raise Protect and lock onto your opponent, while your Trainer stays behind and backs you up with Poké Balls and items.

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge Not released yet Cobblemon 1.8+

Get started Controls

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• 🎮 You drive the Pokémon: WASD, jump and fly at its own Speed, moves on 1-4, Shift to dodge, right click for Protect, Z to lock on.
  • ⚔️ Every kind of fight: wild Pokémon (and the ones that wander in), Cobblemon's NPC trainers, Radical Cobblemon Trainers, and other players, in singles and doubles.
  • 🧪 Moves that do what they do in the games: the real damage formula, stat stages, status, weather, terrain, hazards, abilities and held items.
  • ✨ Mega, Tera, Dynamax and Z-Moves on one key, with Cobblemon: Mega Showdown.
  • 🧱 Moves leave a mark: Ember burns through leaves and Earthquake cracks stone, unless mobGriefing is off or you are inside a marked arena.
  • ⚙️ Every feature can be tuned or switched off with /cac, and the server picks which battles play in real time.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Version 0.1.41 Minecraft 1.21.1 Side Server and every player's game Cobblemon 1.8+ Fabric Fabric Language Kotlin, Architectury API NeoForge Kotlin for Forge, Architectury API Optional Cobblemon: Mega Showdown: Mega Evolution, Tera, Dynamax and Z-Moves in a real-time fight · PokeBelt: throwing Poké Balls mid-fight · Radical Cobblemon Trainers: its trainers fight in real time, and a win still counts

No public download yet. New here? Start with Getting Started.

docs.title: Commands & Configuration
docs.text:
Every command is under /cac and needs operator level 2. Each level of the command answers on its own with what it holds, so the tree can be walked with Tab.

Command What it does /cac format [wild\|npc\|pvp] [singles\|doubles] [on\|off] which battles play in real time /cac config [feature] [setting] [value] switch off and tune each feature /cac reset every setting back to its default /cac reload reread the config file /cac move <move> one move's real-time numbers /cac hit <move> the Pokémon you drive hits its opponent once, with the numbers in chat /cac arena add <name> <from> <to> mark a box where no move breaks a block /cac arena remove <name> · /cac arena list manage the arenas of your dimension /cac debug events print Action Combat's events in your chat (for mod authors) /cachud layout (any player) pick one of three HUD layouts

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Every feature has enabled plus its own settings, saved to the config file as soon as they change:

possession · camera · movement · leash · disconnect · damage · moves · stamina · defense · hud · wild_ai · switch · aggro · bag · lock_on · capture · intrusion · breath · effects · status · field · abilities · held_items · npc · pvp · gimmicks · block_damage

/cac config <feature> lists a feature's settings with their values, and /cac config <feature> <setting> shows the range. A few worth knowing:

Setting Default What it is leash radius 32 blocks your Pokémon may go from your Trainer damage scale 25 how hard hits land, in percent of the games' damage pvp time_limit_seconds 0 (off) the PvP clock npc switch_seconds 10 the least time between an NPC's switches gimmicks dynamax_seconds 20 how long a Dynamax lasts block_damage soft_power / stone_power 60 / 100 the power to break soft blocks and stone

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
While you drive a Pokémon the keys go to it, never to your Trainer. Every key below can be rebound in Options → Controls → Cobblemon Action Combat, except the ones that reuse a vanilla key.

Key What it does W A S D, mouse move and turn, at the Pokémon's own Speed Space jump; a double tap takes off with a species that flies, then Space climbs and sprint dives 1 2 3 4 (the hotbar keys) cast the Pokémon's four moves; a close-range move is only readied Left click (attack) land the readied close-range move on an opponent in reach Shift (sneak) dodge: a 4-block dash, with a moment where nothing hits you Right click (use) Protect: a bubble that blocks every hit for a second and a half Z lock onto an opponent; Tab moves the lock to the next one; Z again lets go Q the battle gimmick: Mega, Tera, Dynamax or Z-Move (see here) H in doubles, swap control to your other Pokémon G (hold) the consumable wheel: scroll to pick a potion, berry or X item, let go to throw it B throw PokeBelt's selected Poké Ball at the locked target; the scroll wheel picks the ball R (Cobblemon's send-out key) tap to switch Pokémon, hold 2 s to run away or forfeit

docs.title: Stamina
docs.text: Moves cost Stamina instead of PP, and so do the dodge, Protect and flying. The bar above the XP bar refills on its own a moment after you stop spending. Run it dry and your Pokémon is exhausted for 3 seconds: it moves at half speed and cannot use moves or take off.

docs.title: The fight HUD
docs.text: Your Pokémon's HP and Stamina sit in one panel, your target's HP in another, and your four moves show their key, cost and cooldown. Damage numbers rise from each hit. /cachud layout picks one of three layouts.

docs.title: The camera
docs.text: The camera sits behind your Pokémon in third person, further back the bigger it is, and F5 is locked for the fight. Your own camera mode comes back when it ends.

docs.title: Community Credits
docs.text:
Action Combat is built on the work of others:

  • Cobblemon, whose Pokémon, battles and data every fight comes from.
  • Pokémon Showdown, whose move, ability and item data seeds every real-time definition.
  • Cobblemon: Mega Showdown, which owns the gimmicks' items, forms and visuals.
  • PokeBelt, which carries the balls thrown mid-fight.
  • Radical Cobblemon Trainers, whose trainers, series and level caps a real-time win still counts toward.

Found a bug or have an idea? Post it in the Discord.

docs.title: Fights
docs.text:
A real-time fight opens in place of the battle Cobblemon would have started. Your lead is thrown out and is yours to drive; your Trainer stays where the fight began, unhurt and ignored by mobs. The fight belongs to the ones in it: nothing outside it (a third player, a mob, an arrow, lava) can hurt its Pokémon, and nobody else can challenge, catch or trade them.

Your Pokémon cannot go more than 32 blocks from your Trainer. At the edge it slides along a lit boundary instead of snapping back.

docs.title: Wild Pokémon
docs.text:
A wild Pokémon fights back with its own moves, by an archetype read from its moveset: most close in to hit, ones with mostly ranged moves keep 6 to 10 blocks away and strafe, and one with nothing to fight with runs. It stands still through each windup while its attack animation plays: that is your opening to dodge. It also dodges some of your attacks.

  • It can start the fight: an aggressive wild Pokémon that attacks you sends your lead out. After a fight, wild hits wait 10 seconds before they can start the next one.
  • Others join in: a hostile wild Pokémon within 16 blocks joins on its own, and any free wild Pokémon your move hits joins too, up to 3 at once. An intruder is a full opponent: it pays EXP and can be caught. Fights against a trainer or a player stay closed.
  • It can run: one that ends up past the 32-block edge gets away.

The fight is won once every wild Pokémon in it is knocked out or caught.

docs.title: Catching
docs.text: With PokeBelt, B makes your Trainer throw the belt's selected ball at the target you locked (or the one you face). It is Cobblemon's own ball and catch rate, so anything that listens to captures still hears it. A wild Pokémon can dodge the ball, half as often as it dodges moves. Catching the last wild Pokémon wins the fight. Without PokeBelt, B tells you a belt is needed.

docs.title: Knock-outs, switching and running
docs.text:
• Your Pokémon faints: it goes back to its ball and a wheel of your party opens. After 2 seconds click one, or press its number. Pick nothing for 30 seconds and the first healthy one goes out. With none left, you lose.
  • Tap R to recall and pick another. Hold R for 2 seconds to run from a wild fight; against a trainer or a player it asks you to hold again, and the second hold forfeits as a loss.
  • EXP and EVs are paid at each knock-out, by Cobblemon's own rules, to every Pokémon you drove in the fight. Level-up moves and evolutions wait for the fight to end.
  • A dropped connection gets 15 seconds of grace: come back and your Pokémon goes out again where it stood.

docs.title: NPC trainers
docs.text: Cobblemon's own NPC trainers send their party out in front of them one at a time (two in doubles), each fighting like a wild Pokémon that never flees. The next comes out 1.5 seconds after one faints. They switch out of a bad type matchup, or under 25 % HP for a healthier Pokémon, at most once every 10 seconds. Beating the whole party wins.

docs.title: RCT trainers
docs.text:
With Radical Cobblemon Trainers, its trainers fight the same way, and the fight still counts in RCT:

  • a win adds the trainer to your progress, moves the series on, raises your level cap and drops its loot;
  • a loss counts nothing and starts the trainer's cooldown;
  • a fight with no winner (you ran, walked away, the server stopped) frees the trainer again.

The trainer's datapack win commands are not run in a real-time fight. If a future RCT version changes what Action Combat calls, the server log says so once and RCT battles go back to turn-based.

docs.title: Player against player
docs.text: Both players drive their Pokémon. With /cac config pvp time_limit_seconds above 0 the fight ends at the limit: the side with more Pokémon standing wins, then the one with more HP left, and a full tie is a draw. Warnings come a minute, 30 and 10 seconds before. Off by default.

docs.title: Doubles
docs.text: Each Trainer drives one Pokémon and an ally AI runs the next healthy one beside it. H swaps control and camera between the two, and when the one you drive faints, control goes to the ally at once. The spread moves that hit the partner in the games (Earthquake, Surf, Explosion, Discharge...) hit your partner in the blast too.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Action Combat targets Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric and NeoForge, with Cobblemon 1.8.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Dependency Notes Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric Loader or NeoForge the jar for your loader Fabric Language Kotlin or Kotlin for Forge the one for your loader Architectury API both loaders Cobblemon 1.8

Optional, each adding something when it is there:

  • Cobblemon: Mega Showdown: Mega Evolution, Terastallization, Dynamax and Z-Moves in a real-time fight (Battle gimmicks).
  • PokeBelt: the only way to throw a Poké Ball in the middle of a fight (Catching).
  • Radical Cobblemon Trainers: its trainers fight in real time and a win still counts there (RCT trainers).
  • Synchro Machine: a player morphed into a Pokémon keeps the turn-based battle.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Cobblemon and the libraries for your loader.
  2. Drop the Action Combat jar for your loader into mods/. Never put both loaders' jars in.
  3. On a server, install it on the server and on every player's game. A client without it, or on another version, is refused at login with a message saying so.
  4. Start a battle the way you always do: throw your Pokémon at a wild one, talk to a trainer, or challenge a player. A gold "Real-time fight!" line says it is yours to drive.

docs.title: Which battles play in real time
docs.text:
The server decides, per kind of battle and per size, with /cac format:

/cac format wild singles on
/cac format npc doubles off
/cac format pvp singles on

A battle the server leaves turn-based opens Cobblemon's normal battle screen. Triples, multi and free-for-all battles are always turn-based. See Commands & Configuration.

docs.title: Moves & Effects
docs.text: Every one of the moves Cobblemon knows has a real-time definition derived from the games' data, and a datapack can change any of it. /cac move <move> shows one move's numbers.

docs.title: How a move goes off
docs.text:
Kind Examples What it does Close range Tackle, Close Combat its key readies it for 3 s; a left click on an opponent in reach lands it when its windup ends Projectile Thunderbolt, Ember flies from your Pokémon where you look; it can be outrun or sidestepped Zone Thunder, Blizzard falls on the spot you aim at a moment later, a ring marking where Area Earthquake, Surf hits everything around you Self and status Swords Dance, Thunder Wave cast for a moment first; a flinch or a heavy hit breaks the cast

A readied close-range move is outlined on the HUD. Its Stamina and cooldown are paid on the click, a click with nothing in reach keeps it readied, and its key again lets it go.

Faster moves start sooner, so Quick Attack comes out well ahead of Tackle. A move that can miss in the games sometimes fumbles instead: the animation plays and nothing happens. Stamina cost and cooldown grow with a move's power, so a stronger move is a bigger hit per press, and a short recovery follows every move.

docs.title: Damage
docs.text: Damage follows the main series formula: level, power, Attack against Defense, the 85–100 % roll, STAB, the type chart, critical hits and stat stages, scaled so an even level-50 duel lasts about 35 seconds per Pokémon. It comes off the Pokémon's real HP.

docs.title: Secondary effects and status
docs.text:
• Stat stages up to ±6, cleared when the Pokémon is recalled; drain, recoil, multi-hit (2-5 at the games' odds), healing, recharge (Hyper Beam stuns for 2 s) and two-turn moves (out of reach while flying or digging).
  • Burn, poison and paralysis as Cobblemon's own status: burn and poison chip HP every 3 s, burn halves physical damage and drains Stamina, paralysis halves the pace and fails 25 % of moves.
  • Sleep and freeze hold the Pokémon still for about 5 and 6 seconds, and each press of a move key shakes some of it off; confusion makes a third of its moves hit itself; a flinch breaks a cast.
  • Weather, terrain, screens and hazards, inside the fight only: rain and sun scale Water and Fire, sandstorm chips, a terrain boosts its type, Reflect and Light Screen halve damage, and Stealth Rock, Spikes, Toxic Spikes and Sticky Web hit every Pokémon sent out after them. Side conditions like Tailwind and Safeguard show their timer but do nothing yet.
  • About 250 moves run special logic of their own in the games; in a real-time fight they do their base damage and whatever effects their data lists.

docs.title: Abilities and held items
docs.text: Damage abilities and items work as in the games (Huge Power, Adaptability, Technician, Sheer Force, Choice Band and Specs, Life Orb, Expert Belt, type-boosting items and plates), and so do contact and on-hit triggers (Static, Flame Body, Rough Skin, Rocky Helmet, Intimidate, Focus Sash, Sitrus Berry, Weakness Policy) and field ones (Drizzle, Drought, Sand Stream, Snow Warning, Swift Swim, Chlorophyll, Levitate, Leftovers, Black Sludge). Every other held item's tooltip says it is inactive in a real-time fight; it still works in turn-based battles.

docs.title: Under water
docs.text: A land Pokémon has 10 seconds of air under water, then loses 5 % of its HP each second until it comes up. Water types and water-breathers never run out, and Fire types are hurt by water.

docs.title: Battle gimmicks
docs.text:
With Cobblemon: Mega Showdown, Q uses the one battle gimmick each Trainer gets per fight. It picks by what the Pokémon holds and the key item you wear:

Gimmick Needs What it does Z-Move a Z-Crystal, a Z-Ring arms the next move of the crystal's type as its Z-Move, once Mega Evolution its Mega Stone, a Mega Bracelet Mega stats and ability; nothing hits it while it changes Terastallization a Tera Orb defends as its Tera type, keeps STAB on its own types, ×2 STAB on a Tera type it had Dynamax a Dynamax Band 20 s bigger, taking half damage, its moves Max Moves with their weather, terrain or stat change; Gigantamax Factor shows the G-Max form

Every form and size goes back when the fight ends; a Dynamax ends early if the Pokémon is recalled. Without Mega Showdown, Q does nothing. G-Max-specific moves are not in: a Gigantamax Pokémon uses Max Moves.

docs.title: Block damage
docs.text:
Moves break the blocks where they land: a projectile where it stops, a zone move where it falls, an area move around its user (never the ground under it).

Block Breaks with Fragile (leaves, flowers, glass, ice, snow, grass, cobwebs) any damaging move: Ember burns through leaves Soft (dirt, sand, gravel, wool) a move of power 60 or more Stone, wood, ores a move of power 100 or more Anything harder, anything with a block entity (chests, furnaces) never

At most 12 blocks per hit, within 2 blocks of the impact, and they drop as a creeper's do. Nothing breaks with the mobGriefing game rule off, with the feature switched off, or inside an arena: /cac arena add <name> <from> <to> marks a box where nothing gives. Pack authors can add blocks to the #cobblemon_action_combat:fragile and #cobblemon_action_combat:unbreakable tags.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If yours is not here, post it in the Discord: it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: My battle opened the normal battle screen
docs.text: The server has that kind of battle turn-based: check /cac format. Triples, multi and free-for-all battles are always turn-based, and so is a battle with a player morphed with Synchro Machine.

docs.title: I was refused at login
docs.text: The server runs Action Combat and your game does not, or runs another version. Install the same version as the server.

docs.title: Q does nothing
docs.text: It needs Cobblemon: Mega Showdown, the right held item and key item (Battle gimmicks), and it works once per fight. The chat line says which.

docs.title: B says I need a belt
docs.text: Throwing a ball mid-fight needs PokeBelt (Catching), and only works in a wild fight.

docs.title: Moves do not break anything
docs.text: The mobGriefing game rule is off, block_damage is switched off, you are inside an arena (/cac arena list), or the move is not strong enough for that block (Block damage).

docs.title: An RCT trainer's battle is turn-based
docs.text: The server log says why at start: RCT's version changed what Action Combat calls. Also check /cac format npc.
